newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's new 7-yr bond yield declines on results.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's new 7-yr bond yield declines on results.

text.p: The yield on Malaysia's new seven-year government bond dropped immediately after results of the issue were announced by Bank Negara on Friday, dealers said.
They said in just half-an-hour after the results were announced, the yield dropped to a low of 6.487 percent against an average issue coupon of 6.586 percent.
But, it recovered partially soon after to settle around 6.523 percent, the dealers said.
"Many were caught short after the issue. That is why the price went up," said a dealer with a large Malaysian bank.
He said the bond was trading around 100.30/35 ringgit after hitting a high of 100.55. It opened at around 100.15.
Around 0810 GMT, Bank Negara said it accepted bids at an average coupon of 6.586 percent for the two billion ringgit seven-year bonds.
The bids were in the range of 6.60 and 6.56 percent.
